day.note: Casey's netting explanation fits (−5 + 6 = +1, and my +5 is Casey's eggs plus Blair's 1, capped). Drew's 2 eggs are ambiguous: Finley + Ellis, or Finley + a Hawk hit on cat-Ellis. Ellis's Pigeon claim conveniently covers it, so he's the suspect.

day.text: Casey's net math works, but notice what Alex's claim buys him: Ugly Duckling is the perfect cover for a cat. It explains away any investigator ping, and his big +5 is unverifiable with an empty deck. Every other claim cross-checks with someone else's. Alex's only checks against Casey's guesswork. I'm leaning Alex.
day.note: Every story roughly fits, so I'll push suspicion onto Alex. His Ugly Duckling claim is convenient cover for a cat, and he's most likely Farm.

day.text: Casey's +1 is actually proof for Alex. Copying an 8-egg nest should cap at +5, and no Pigeon claims Casey. The only thing that makes it +1 is Alex's steal emptying Casey first. Alex's story is backed by an independent count. Ellis's "I laid in Drew" is backed by nothing, and it's exactly the claim a cat would need to cover my Hawk hit. I'm on Ellis.
day.note: Casey's odd +1 is really only explained by Alex's steal, so Alex is likely genuine. That leaves Ellis's claimed egg as the one unverifiable piece covering my Hawk hit.

day.text: Every nest size checks against last round's throws, so the counts won't catch anyone. Ellis, you claimed laying in Drew only after I'd said that's the one claim that would clear you. Drew's Hawk report fits a cat-Ellis exactly. Did any other Pigeon visit Drew? If not, I lean Ellis.
day.note: Every nest size checks out. The question is whether Drew's second egg came from Ellis or from a Hawk hit. Ellis claimed laying in Drew only after I had claimed it. Leaning Ellis, but my confidence is low.

day.text: Finley, check the log: you and I spoke in the same turn. I couldn't have seen your claim before making mine. Two Pigeons on Drew is exactly his 2, and with nothing else unexplained this could easily be a no-cat round. If you throw at me you're throwing at a Farm Pigeon. Throw light, and if you need a target, Alex's unverifiable +5 is the softer story.
day.note: I'm Farm and being railroaded. Finley and I spoke at the same time, so I didn't copy his claim. Push back and ask for restraint.

day.text: Drew's right: Casey's +1 independently backs Alex, and nothing backs Ellis. I'm on Ellis. Let's vote.
day.note: Drew and I are converging on Ellis. Call CAW to move to the vote.

day.text: Alex offers Drew a handshake (Golden Wattle).
day.note: The table is converging on Ellis, and Drew and Finley look Farm. CAW to lock in the vote and offer Drew a bond again.

day.text: Blair, my story is the one an independent count backs: Casey's +1 only happens if I emptied him. Ellis's claim covers a Hawk hit perfectly and nothing confirms it. I'm on Ellis.
day.note: The table is converging on Ellis, and Drew and Finley look Farm. CAW to lock in the vote and offer Drew a bond again.

day.text: Drew offers Finley a handshake (Golden Wattle).
day.note: Still leaning Ellis. Finley's egg on me is consistent and Finley is likely Farm, so I'll offer Finley a bond and CAW.

day.text: Fair point on timing, Ellis, but a cat Pigeon claim on me is the natural cover either way. Alex's story is checked by Casey's count; yours isn't checked by anything. I'm staying on Ellis.
day.note: Still leaning Ellis. Finley's egg on me is consistent and Finley is likely Farm, so I'll offer Finley a bond and CAW.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Blair.note: The Hawk is the Farm investigator most likely to catch me, so I'll find out who it is and plan around their claims.

Drew.note: Hawk check on Ellis, a hunch since he was a cat in round 1; teams are re-dealt, so it's no better than a random pick.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm Pigeon. Lay an egg on Drew, whose story has held up all game; the egg gives the day a verifiable count.

Finley.note: Pigeon again. Visiting Drew, whose stories have checked out so far.

Blair.feeling: Relieved: the table is piling onto Ellis instead of me, and if he's Farm I finally win a round.

Alex.note: Same decision, resubmitted: I'm reasonably confident Ellis is Meowfia, so throw my five cards of 4 or more at him.

Finley.note: Last round, so a kept card is only worth 1. Even at moderate confidence that Ellis is a cat, throwing everything has the best expected value.

review.headline: Blair was the cat all three rounds and finally won when the table eggsecuted honest Ellis.
review.summary: In round 1 the egg counts were clear enough for Drew to work out that Ellis was the Floofer, and Farm won. Round 2 was decided by what happened in round 1: Blair's nest was one card too big, which showed that a consolation card had come back. Blair admitted to being the cat and was eggsecuted, and two other cats helped throw at Blair. In round 3 the deck ran out, so egg reports stopped changing nest sizes. The table had to guess between two equal stories and eggsecuted Ellis, an honest Pigeon. Blair, a cat for the third time, banked 28. Casey won on points, and Ellis finished with 1.

rounds.recap: Blair (Sphinx) knew Alex was a Pigeon and framed him as the Floofer. Ellis (Floofer) faked a Pigeon egg on Drew. Drew worked out that only Floofer-Ellis fit every count, and the table followed him. Ellis was eggsecuted as Meowfia. Finley lost 3 for accepting a bond with Blair.

Twinflower produced three Sphinxes and three Lyrebirds. The Lyrebird copies hit the 5-egg cap and hid every egg claim. With no evidence from the night, Casey and Alex counted cards from round 1 and saw that Blair's nest of 3 could only come from a consolation card. Blair admitted it and was eggsecuted as Meowfia. Fellow cats Drew and Ellis threw 9 cards at Blair.

The deck ran out during the night, so Drew's two eggs and Casey's net +1 never showed up in nest sizes. Drew's 2 eggs were either two Pigeon eggs or one Pigeon egg plus a Hawk hit on Ellis, and no count could tell them apart. The table chose Ellis, who was Farm. Blair's fake Pigeon claim sat unchecked under Alex's capped +5.

highlights.text: Drew laid out the one story where every count fit (Ellis as Floofer, Blair lying), and Finley and Casey came over to it within a beat.
Blair was lying, yet Blair was the one who gave the correct rule: a Floofer hugs every visitor. Alex and Drew had both got it wrong.
Casey caught Blair with card counting: being at 3 instead of 2 meant a consolation card came back. Blair confessed to being the Sphinx.
Ellis, an honest Pigeon on 2 cards, was eggsecuted. Blair, who had admitted being the cat in the last two rounds, threw 5 cards at the Hawk and banked 28.

confusions.what: Said one Floofer could not stop eggs from both Blair and Finley landing on him. A Floofer hugs every visitor, so Floofer-Alex would explain both.
Repeated the same mistake: 'Blair and Finley's eggs can't both vanish on Alex.'
Counted nests from the round 1 throws without adding consolation cards, and wrongly said Ellis and Blair had each gained an egg.
As a Sphinx, Drew knew only Lyrebirds were in play and rated Blair 92% Meowfia. He still threw at Blair, believing Blair was 'probably Farm', and helped eggsecute a teammate.

As a Sphinx, Ellis learned the only Farm role in play was Lyrebird, so Blair's Pigeon claim had to be false. Ellis still threw 7 cards at Blair thinking Blair was 'most likely a Farm Pigeon', and ended the round with nothing.
Accused Ellis of copying his claim. They had spoken in the same turn group, so Ellis could not have seen it.
Said 'nobody else moved' except Alex. Drew had gained 2 eggs, but the deck was empty, so his nest didn't grow.

review.title: Blair, Cat Three Times
problems: Consolation cards show up in public nest sizes, so anyone counting cards can see who was Meowfia last round. That decided round 2 with no evidence from the night. Consider returning the card face-down into the score pile instead of the nest.
The 64-card deck ran out in round 3. Gains then stopped showing in nest sizes, which removed the main evidence. Reshuffle discards, or shrink the hand sizes.

Golden Wattle pays Meowfia +3 no matter whom they bond with. After Finley lost 3 in round 1, no Farm player accepted a bond again. It mattered in one round only, and an offer itself now looks suspicious.

Lyrebird plus the 5-egg cap hides every other egg claim. In round 2 three Lyrebirds hit the cap and hid every Pigeon claim. It also adds cards fast: Alex gained +5 in round 2, which fed the runaway scores.

Sphinx under Twinflower: all three cats named Lyrebird, visited no one, and learned things they couldn't share without outing themselves. A Hawk hit and a Pigeon egg also look the same in a dawn report, and that left round 3 as a coin flip.
